answers.note: Tight 25-minute sheet that mixes perfect tense, family words and opinions, with a full answer key, though the opinion task is not linked to the perfect tense or family theme.
Strongest design: from-memory retrieval, error-spotting and production tying family plus perfect tense plus opinion, with a parent role (listen and tick) any parent can do.
Well supported for parents and teacher, but the word table at the top hands over every answer to Tasks 1 and 2, so much of it is copying rather than recall.
Complete day-by-day plan for all three weeks with 25-minute active blocks, clear spacing, lighter football evenings and built-in spare blocks.
Sensible weighting and spacing, but the weekly grid labels blocks only by subject and Week 3 asks for full timed papers far beyond the student's 30-minute limit.
Only Week 1 is actually planned; Weeks 2 and 3 are one vague line each, so spacing and specific active tasks are mostly asserted rather than shown.
Opens with retrieval on exactly the two gaps, models charge balancing before faded and independent practice, and ends with exit check, homework and student and parent notes.

Excellent modelling and practice on melting points, but the starter retrieves formulae and not the melting-point explanation, which is then re-taught, and the homework review is not clearly used to shape next steps.
Thorough chemistry, but the starter re-tests what she already got right rather than her gaps, the hour splits across three focuses, and there is no note for the student or parent.
